module_title: Advanced MS Office Shortcuts - Function Keys and Power Tools
introduction: Tailored for SSC CGL Tier-2 (Mains) and technical exams, this advanced module covers complex function key bindings, MS Excel power tools, and advanced formatting commands.

core_concepts.title: Advanced MS Word Formatting
core_concepts.description:
- `Shift + F3`: Toggle Change Case (Switches instantly between lowercase, UPPERCASE, and Sentence case).
- `Ctrl + Shift + >`: Increase font size.
- `Ctrl + Shift + <`: Decrease font size.
- `Ctrl + Enter`: Insert a Page Break (forces text to start on the next page).

core_concepts.title: Advanced Saving Mechanics
core_concepts.description: - `F12`: Open the 'Save As' dialog box (allows you to save an existing file with a new name or in a new format like PDF).

core_concepts.title: Excel Power Shortcuts
core_concepts.description:
- `F2`: Edit the active cell (places the cursor directly inside the cell).
- `Ctrl + 1`: Open the 'Format Cells' dialog box.
- `Alt + =` (Alt plus Equals): Instantly apply the AutoSum formula to a column or row of numbers.

core_concepts.title: PowerPoint Specifics
core_concepts.description:
- `F5`: Start the Slideshow from the very first (beginning) slide.
- `Shift + F5`: Start the Slideshow directly from the current active slide.

important_entities.name: Save vs. Save As
important_entities.significance: `Ctrl + S` overwrites the current file silently. `F12` actively opens the 'Save As' menu so you can create a completely separate copy of the file under a different name.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: In a Web Browser, `F5` means 'Refresh the page'. However, in MS PowerPoint, `F5` means 'Start Slideshow'. Read the exam question carefully to see which software they are asking about.
If asked how to modify data inside an Excel cell without double-clicking the mouse, the answer is strictly `F2`. Many candidates guess 'Enter', which simply moves you down to the next cell.

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: Alt + Equals gives you the Total
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: In Excel, 'Equals' (=) is the start of every formula. `Alt + =` automatically writes the `=SUM()` formula for you.

exam_strategy_tips: For Tier-2 Mains, `F12` (Save As) and `Shift + F3` (Change Case) are extremely high-yield targets. Ensure you know the difference between starting a presentation from the beginning (`F5`) versus the current slide (`Shift + F5`).
